module purpose: neorv32_debug_dtm samples the JTAG pins (jtag_tck_i, jtag_tdi_i, jtag_tms_i) into clk_i-synchronous registers, runs the TAP controller state machine, captures and shifts an instruction register and the IDCODE, DTMCS, DMI and bypass data registers between jtag_tdi_i and jtag_tdo_o, and on a data-register update issues a DMI read or write request (operation, address, write data) on dmi_req_o, captures the response data from dmi_rsp_i, and tracks busy, error and DMI reset status.

use-case flows.value: JTAG pin values (TCK, TDI, TMS) sampled into clk_i-synchronous registers, with TCK rising and falling edges detected
TAP controller state advanced on each synchronized TCK rising edge according to TMS
instruction register loaded with the IDCODE instruction in LOGIC_RESET or IR_CAPTURE and shifted from TDI in IR_SHIFT
selected data register (IDCODE, DTMCS status, DMI response, bypass) captured, shifted and returned bit by bit on jtag_tdo_o, or the instruction bits during IR_SHIFT
one-cycle data-register update pulse derived from entry into DR_UPDATE
DMI read or write request (operation, address, write data) taken from the DMI scan register on an update while idle and driven to the debug module
pending DMI access: response data captured while busy, busy cleared on acknowledge
DMI reset and hard-reset requests taken from DTMCS bits 16 and 17 on an update, cleared when idle
DMI overrun error flag set by an update during a pending access, cleared by a DMI reset, reported in the DMI and DTMCS capture values
all registers cleared while rstn_i is low, TAP state forced to LOGIC_RESET and the DMI hard-reset request set to 1

conceptual assets.concept: TAP controller state -- the JTAG protocol phase that decides when the instruction and data registers are captured, shifted and updated
conceptual assets.reasoning: The sequencing flow updates tap_ctrl_state on each synchronized TCK rising edge according to TMS (lines 121-138) and forces LOGIC_RESET on an illegal encoding (line 139) and on rstn_i (line 119). Its value decides the IR load and shift (GATES tap_reg.ireg, lines 178, 180), the DR capture and shift (GATES tap_reg.idcode, dtmcs, dmi and bypass, lines 185, 192), the TDO source (GATES jtag_tdo_o, line 203) and the update pulse (GATES dr_trigger.sreg, line 151). Integrity is Established: a wrong state captures, shifts or commits the wrong register, and a spurious DR_UPDATE produces the pulse that issues a DMI request (lines 151-161, 265). Availability is Established under the implemented conditions: the state is held between TCK edges, and LOGIC_RESET is reached by reset (line 119) or by TMS high on successive edges (lines 124, 125, 132). tap_ctrl_state stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4, line 123; self-updating). jtag_tms_i sets: this entity reads it to store it (SOURCES tap_sync.tms_ff, occurrence 2, line 101), and the synchronized bit decides every transition. Not listed: tap_sync.tms_ff, whose records only pass the bit to itself and to tap_sync.tms; tap_sync.tms, which only gates the transitions (DERIVES_FROM tap_sync.tms_ff, line 110); and tap_sync.tck_ff, tap_sync.tck_rising and tap_sync.tck_falling, the edge strobes derived from jtag_tck_i that only time updates of other elements (lines 106-107, 121, 202). jtag_tck_i is excluded as an input that only enables the clocking of other logic.

conceptual assets.concept: Selected JTAG instruction -- which data register a scan reaches and which DMI or DTMCS update applies
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure flow loads tap_reg.ireg with addr_idcode_c in LOGIC_RESET or IR_CAPTURE (lines 178-179) and shifts the TDI bit into it in IR_SHIFT (line 181). The held instruction selects the data register captured and shifted (SELECTS at lines 186 and 193), selects the TDO source (SELECTS jtag_tdo_o, line 206), and qualifies the DTMCS reset update (GATES, line 247), the DMI request issue (GATES, line 265) and the overrun error (GATES, line 258). Integrity is Established: a wrong instruction routes a scan to another register or commits a DMI request or reset that the scan did not address. Availability is Established for holding the instruction between IR scans (lines 178-181). tap_reg.ireg stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4, line 181). jtag_tdi_i sets: the instruction bits enter there and this entity stores them (SOURCES tap_sync.tdi_ff, occurrence 2, line 100). jtag_tdo_o is an exit port: the instruction bits leave during IR_SHIFT (DERIVES_FROM tap_reg.ireg, occurrence 3, line 204). tap_sync.tdi_ff and tap_sync.tdi only forward the TDI bit (lines 100, 111). tap_reg.bypass, selected by any other instruction, only returns the TDI bit one shift later (COPIES tap_sync.tdi, line 197; CARRIES jtag_tdo_o, line 210): it forwards the requester's own data and holds no state, setting or decision of its own, so it is not reported.

conceptual assets.concept: Data-register update commit -- the one-cycle decision that a completed scan is applied
conceptual assets.reasoning: dr_trigger.sreg records whether the TAP is in DR_UPDATE (lines 151-156), and dr_trigger.valid is 1 when dr_trigger.sreg equals 01 (line 161): one pulse per entry into DR_UPDATE. Every commit depends on this decision: the DTMCS reset bits are applied (GATES, line 247), a DMI request is issued and busy set (GATES, line 265; line 270), and an update during a pending access is flagged as an error (GATES, line 258). Integrity is Established: a spurious pulse issues a DMI access or reset that no completed scan requested, and a missing one drops the scanned request. dr_trigger.valid computes the decision (GATED_BY dr_trigger.sreg, occurrence 2, line 161). dr_trigger.sreg is the condition operand that holds the DR_UPDATE history (GATES dr_trigger.valid, line 161), not the decision; tap_ctrl_state is listed under the TAP state concept.

conceptual assets.concept: DMI request presented to the debug module -- operation, register address and write data
conceptual assets.reasoning: When idle and not in hard reset, an update pulse with ireg = addr_dmi_c (lines 264-265) takes the address and write-data slices of tap_reg.dmi into dmi_ctrl.addr and dmi_ctrl.wdata (lines 266-267) and, only for a read or write code, the operation into dmi_ctrl.op (lines 268-269); op returns to dmi_req_nop_c on every other cycle (line 263). These fields drive dmi_req_o (lines 283-285). The debug module that consumes them is not supplied, so Integrity is Established from these delivering lines: it must receive exactly the operation, address and data that were scanned in and committed. Availability is conditional on busy, dmihardreset and the update pulse, and is not claimed unconditionally. dmi_req_o carries complete request transactions (op, addr, data) and dmi_rsp_i the matching response (data, ack): both are transport records, so the stored fields inside the block are the references. dmi_ctrl.op (occurrence 4, line 269), dmi_ctrl.addr (occurrence 4, line 266) and dmi_ctrl.wdata (occurrence 3, line 267) store (CLOCKED_BY clk_i), and each CARRIES its dmi_req_o field (lines 283-285). jtag_tdi_i sets: the request bits enter there (SOURCES tap_sync.tdi_ff, occurrence 2, line 100) before being shifted into tap_reg.dmi (line 196). tap_reg.dmi is listed under the DMI scan value concept: the committed request is a distinct value, taken only under the qualified update and held while tap_reg.dmi is recaptured and shifted.

conceptual assets.concept: DMI access in progress -- the pending-transaction state
conceptual assets.reasoning: dmi_ctrl.busy is set when a read or write request is issued (line 270) and cleared when dmi_rsp_i.ack is 1 (lines 275-276). It blocks a new request (GATES dmi_ctrl.addr, op and wdata, line 264), enables capture of the response data (GATES dmi_ctrl.rdata, lines 273-274), lets the DMI reset bits clear only when idle (GATES, line 250) and turns an update during a pending access into an error (GATES dmi_ctrl.err, line 258). Integrity is Established: a wrong busy value lets a second request overwrite the pending operation, address and data, or loses the response. Availability depends on the acknowledge from outside this file and is not claimed unconditionally. dmi_ctrl.busy stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 6, line 270). dmi_rsp_i.ack enters through a transport record and is not reported.

conceptual assets.concept: DMI overrun error status -- whether a request arrived while an access was pending
conceptual assets.reasoning: dmi_ctrl.err is set when an update with ireg = addr_dmi_c arrives while busy (lines 258-259) and cleared by dmireset or dmihardreset (lines 256-257). It is reported to the JTAG requester as the two low bits of dmi_nxt (line 229) and as dtmcs_nxt bits 11-10 (line 224), captured into tap_reg.dmi and tap_reg.dtmcs (lines 188-189) and shifted out on jtag_tdo_o (lines 208-209). Integrity is Established: the requester learns that a request was dropped only through this flag, so it must follow lines 256-259. dmi_ctrl.err computes the decision (GATED_BY dmi_ctrl.busy, occurrence 5, line 259). jtag_tdo_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM tap_reg.dmi, occurrence 6, line 209). tap_reg.dmi and tap_reg.dtmcs, which also hold the captured error bits, are listed under their read-out concepts; tap_reg.dmi_nxt and tap_reg.dtmcs_nxt only assemble the capture values.

conceptual assets.concept: DMI reset and hard-reset requests held for the DMI controller
conceptual assets.reasoning: On an update pulse with ireg = addr_dtmcs_c, dmi_ctrl.dmireset and dmi_ctrl.dmihardreset take DTMCS bits 16 and 17 scanned in by the requester (lines 247-249); otherwise they clear while idle (lines 250-252), and dmihardreset is 1 after rstn_i (line 239). Both clear the error flag (GATES dmi_ctrl.err, line 256), dmihardreset blocks request issue (GATES, line 265), and both are reported in dtmcs_nxt bits 17 and 16 (lines 220-221). Integrity is Established: a forced bit clears the error or suppresses DMI requests, and a lost bit leaves the error set. dmi_ctrl.dmihardreset (occurrence 4, line 249) and dmi_ctrl.dmireset (occurrence 4, line 248) store (CLOCKED_BY clk_i). jtag_tdi_i sets: the command bits enter there (SOURCES tap_sync.tdi_ff, occurrence 2, line 100) before being shifted into tap_reg.dtmcs (line 195). tap_reg.dtmcs is listed under the DTMCS concept; tap_reg.dtmcs_nxt only returns these bits to the capture (COPIES, lines 220-221).

conceptual assets.concept: DTM control and status word returned to and written by the JTAG requester
conceptual assets.reasoning: In DR_CAPTURE with ireg = addr_dtmcs_c, tap_reg.dtmcs takes dtmcs_nxt (line 188): the DMI reset bits (lines 220-221), the error status (line 224) and fixed fields (lines 219, 222-223, 225-226). DR_SHIFT shifts TDI through it (line 195) and jtag_tdo_o returns its bit 0 on each falling TCK edge (line 208); bits 16 and 17 of the shifted-in value become the DMI reset requests at update (lines 248-249). Integrity is Established: the requester outside this file must receive exactly the captured status on jtag_tdo_o, and the command bits applied must be those shifted in. tap_reg.dtmcs stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3, line 188); its records show that use (SOURCES jtag_tdo_o, line 208; SOURCES dmi_ctrl.dmireset, line 248). jtag_tdo_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM tap_reg.dtmcs, occurrence 5, line 208).

conceptual assets.concept: DMI scan value -- the response (address, read data, error) captured for read-out and the request scanned in
conceptual assets.reasoning: In DR_CAPTURE with ireg = addr_dmi_c, tap_reg.dmi takes dmi_nxt, the concatenation of dmi_ctrl.addr, dmi_ctrl.rdata and the error bits (lines 189, 229). DR_SHIFT shifts TDI through it (line 196), jtag_tdo_o returns bit 0 on each falling TCK edge (line 209), and at update its operation field decides whether a request starts (GATES dmi_ctrl.busy and dmi_ctrl.op, line 268) while its slices become the request (lines 266-269). Integrity is Established: the read data returned by the debug module (line 274) reaches the requester only through this capture and shift, and the request is taken from these bits. tap_reg.dmi stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3, line 189). jtag_tdo_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM tap_reg.dmi, occurrence 6, line 209). jtag_tdi_i sets (SOURCES tap_sync.tdi_ff, occurrence 2, line 100). dmi_ctrl.rdata captures dmi_rsp_i.data unchanged (COPIES, line 274) and its only use record is SOURCES tap_reg.dmi_nxt (line 229), an internal element: it holds one step of the value tap_reg.dmi carries on and is secondary. dmi_rsp_i is a transport record.

conceptual assets.concept: Device identification code returned over JTAG
conceptual assets.reasoning: In DR_CAPTURE with ireg = addr_idcode_c, the instruction loaded after LOGIC_RESET or IR_CAPTURE (lines 178-179), tap_reg.idcode is loaded with IDCODE_VERSION & IDCODE_PARTID & IDCODE_MANID & '1' (line 187), shifted in DR_SHIFT (line 194) and returned on jtag_tdo_o (line 207). The requester that reads it is outside this file, so Integrity is Established from these delivering lines: it must receive exactly the identification value built from the generics. No line restricts who reads it, so confidentiality is not established. tap_reg.idcode stores (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3, line 187; SOURCES jtag_tdo_o, line 207). jtag_tdo_o is the exit port (DERIVES_FROM tap_reg.idcode, occurrence 4, line 207).
